page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a high-performance computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a high-speed 150 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance, particularly in multi-core and memory-bound operations. The instance achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 695.05 GB/sec and write speeds at 347.3 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10% of tested servers. Single-core performance remains strong, placing in the top 25% across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, while specialized workloads like software compilation with Clang and PassMark physics simulations also register top-tier results.

The primary tradeoff of the hpc7a.24xlarge is the complete absence of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators, making it unsuitable for local-storage-heavy databases or GPU-dependent deep learning. However, the combination of dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores, massive DDR5 memory bandwidth, and 150 Gbps networking makes it highly cost-efficient for distributed high-performance computing workloads. It is exceptionally well-suited for molecular modeling, computational fluid dynamics, large-scale physics simulations, memory-intensive scientific computing, and parallel software compilation.
